cards.text: Here the prophet is praying for God’s people, and he opens BIG: “I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts.” He’s looking back at the many good things the LORD has done for the house of Israel. Friend, this man did not walk in with a sticky note. He walked in with a SCROLL.

cards.question: God said of Israel, “They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal.” So what did He become for them?
When Israel was in distress, the LORD kept His distance from it.

cards.text: In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old. Friend, I use my mustache for hands and I STILL drop a cookie box on a good day, and He carried a whole NATION.
Then comes the turn nobody wants. Israel rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit.

cards.question: After Israel rebelled, the LORD turned and became their ___.

cards.text: Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses. I bet it’s like finding an old photo of yourself smiling and going, “Wait. What happened to THAT guy?”

cards.question: Remembering Moses, they ask where the One is who brought them through the ___.

cards.text: Where is the One who set His Holy Spirit among them? Where is the One who sent His glorious arm to lead them by the right hand of Moses and divided the waters before them?

cards.question: The prayer gives a reason the LORD divided the waters before His people. What is it?

answers.text: To gain for Himself everlasting renown
To see whether they would trust Moses
To give the people a shortcut home

cards.question: The LORD led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, and they kept stumbling the whole way.

cards.text: Like cattle going down to the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. And the prophet tells the LORD He led His people this way to make for Himself a glorious name.

Then the prayer looks up: “Look down from heaven and see.” Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer hoping somebody would open it and SEE me, so I feel that line all the way down to my gold base.

cards.question: The one praying asks where God’s zeal and might are. What does he say about God’s compassion for him right now?

answers.text: It was given to his enemies

cards.text: Then a hard line: Abraham, the forefather of the nation, does not know them, and Israel does not acknowledge them. Their own family tree is leaving them on READ.

cards.question: Even so, the prayer tells the LORD that He is their ___, their Redeemer from Everlasting.
The prayer asks the LORD why He makes them stray from His ways and hardens their hearts. Then it asks Him to do something for the sake of His servants. What?
The prayer says God’s people possessed His holy place for only a short while, and now enemies have trampled His sanctuary.

cards.text: Now they say they’ve become like those He never ruled, like those not called by His name. Friend, that is the sound of a people who feel FORGOTTEN.
Now the prayer gets LOUD. It begs the LORD to rend the heavens and come down so the mountains would quake at His presence, and friend, this is NOT “call me back when you get a minute.”

cards.question: The prayer says God coming down would be like fire making water boil. Who would it make His name known to?

cards.text: And He’s done it before. When He did awesome works they did not expect, He came down, and the mountains trembled at His presence.

cards.question: The prayer says no eye has ever seen any God besides the LORD, who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.

cards.text: The LORD welcomes those who gladly do right and remember His ways. Then the prayer comes clean: “Surely You were angry, for we sinned.”

cards.question: Right after admitting they sinned, what does the prayer ask the LORD?

answers.text: How they can be saved if they stay in their sins
Why He ever chose them to be His people
When their enemies will finally leave the land

cards.question: The prayer says their righteous acts are clean enough to make up for their sins.

cards.text: Each of us has become like something unclean, and all our righteous acts are like filthy rags. Not their WORST stuff, friend. Their BEST stuff.

cards.question: The prayer says no one calls on the LORD’s name or strives to take hold of Him. What does it say the LORD has done with His face?

cards.text: And right in the middle of all that, the prayer turns: “But now, O LORD, You are our Father.” That line again, and I think it lands even harder this time.

cards.question: The prayer paints a picture: the people are the clay, and the LORD is the ___.

cards.text: We are all the work of His hand. Friend, in all my years baking, not ONE ball of dough has ever looked up at me and said, “Papa, actually, I’d rather be a star.”

cards.question: The prayer asks the LORD not to be angry beyond measure, and not to remember their ___ forever.

cards.text: Then the prayer looks around. God’s holy cities have become a wilderness, Zion a wasteland and Jerusalem a desolation.

cards.question: What happened to the holy and beautiful temple where their fathers praised God?

answers.text: It was washed away in a flood
It was taken apart and moved

cards.text: And all that was dear to them lies in ruins. No joke here, friend. This is a people standing in the rubble, still talking to God.

cards.question: The prayer ends by asking the LORD questions.

cards.text: “Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?” That’s where the prayer stops, friend, right on the question.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "I will make known the LORD's loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Look down from heaven and see.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "But now, O LORD, You are our Father.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the opening with the quote, "He's looking back...", "Friend, this man did not walk in with a sticky note." and "He walked in with a SCROLL."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The right answer "To gain for Himself everlasting renown" sounds like the Bible. The wrong answer "To give the people a shortcut home" is casual, modern and close to silly, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: In Isaiah 63:16, "Israel" means the patriarch Jacob, the same way "Abraham" means the forefather. The card says who Abraham is but not who Israel is. The baker will likely read "Israel does not acknowledge them" as the nation.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer "Return" is one word. The wrong answers, "Send them a new leader" and "Wipe out their enemies", are four or five words, so the right answer stands out by length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "That is the sound of a people who feel FORGOTTEN" states a feeling as fact. Isaiah 63:19 says only that they have become like those He never ruled, like those not called by His name. The guess needs to be marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: Feelings. He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: "Each of us...filthy rags.", "Not their WORST stuff, friend." and "Their BEST stuff."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin gives the prayer's first-person words ("Each of us has become... all our righteous acts...") in his own narration, with no quotation marks and no mention of who is speaking. It reads as if Papa Dorin is including himself, and the card then switches to "their".

rule.text: Who's speaking. When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first. For example, "Then the prophet says, 'And I asked…'" (Isa 40:6).

findings.problem: Isaiah 64:8 makes the point that the people belong to God as the work of His hand. The joke's action is dough never objecting to the shape it's given. That is the clay talking back to the potter, which comes from other passages (Isaiah 29:16; 45:9), not from this verse. So the comparison doesn't share the verse's core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: "And all that was dear to them lies in ruins.", "No joke here, friend." and "This is a people standing in the rubble, still talking to God."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
